Affected Gene: Crossover of CYP11B1 promoter with CYP11B2 coding sequence
Pathogenic Effect: Aldosterone synthase expression under control of ACTH-sensitive promoter
Classic Presentation: Severe hyperaldosteronism in childhood or young adults with autosomal dominant inheritance
Targeted Treatment: Low-dose glucocorticoids, to suppress endogenous ACTH production. May need concomitant ARB and/or ENaC inhibitor therapy.

Pathogenic Effect: Gain-of-function mutation in the Cl- channel CIC-2, leading to increased Cl- efflux and subsequent membrane depolarization. Membrane depolarization increases Ca2+ entry, which leads to hyperplasia and increased CYP11B2 expression
Loss of Na+selectivity of K+ channel, GIRK4, leading to membrane depolarization, which increases Ca2+ entry and subsequent hyperplasia and increased CYP11B2 expression
Classic Presentation: Severe early-onset hypertension associated with profound hypokalemia
Targeted Treatment: None currently available at present. Macrolide antibiotics are effective in vitro, but in vivo effects have not been well characterized

Pathogenic Effect: Mutation in the pore-forming α1 subunit of the voltage-sensitive calcium channel Cav3.2, leading to increased Ca2+ entry and subsequent hyperplasia and increased CYP11B2 expression
Classic Presentation: Early-onset primary aldosteronism. May be associated with developmental delay or attention deficit disorder
